key: All this, whatsoever exists in the universe, should be covered by the Lord. Having renounced (the unreal), enjoy (the Real). Do not covet the wealth of any man.
s: The Isa opens its eighteen verses, which run from renunciation and work to a prayer at the hour of death; Śaṅkara, commentary on verse 1, reads the covering as seeing all that moves as the Self, from which renunciation follows, and ‘enjoy’ as protect.
src: Śaṅkara, Īśa Upaniṣad Bhāṣya, verse 1, trans. S. Sitarama Sastri, The Upanishads and Sri Sankara’s Commentary, vol. 1 (1905 printing)

evidence.words: All this universe, movable and immovable, unreal in absolute truth* should be covered by his self, the Lord, Paramatnum, with the idea, “ I alone am all this as being the inner self of all. ” … One who thus contemplates on the self as the Paramatman is bound to renounce the three-fold desire of son, etc., and not perforin Karma … Bhnnjithah means protect.
evidence.lang: English (Sitarama Sastri’s translation of the Sanskrit, OCR as printed)
evidence.gloss: The whole universe, moving and unmoving, is to be covered by one’s own Self, the Lord, with the thought ‘I alone am all this, as the inner Self of all’; whoever so contemplates the Self must renounce the threefold desire for son and the rest; bhuñjīthāḥ means protect.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Isa Upanishad 1, at [0]). Plain sense describes the eighteen verses in the day’s own terms: renunciation (1), work (2), and the closing prayers of 15 to 18 with the body burned to ashes (17). Śaṅkara’s commentary on Isa 1 in the packet (Sitarama Sastri) says the universe, moving and unmoving, is to be covered by one’s own Self with the thought ‘I alone am all this’, that one who so contemplates is bound to renounce, and that bhuñjīthāḥ means protect: the reading carries all three claims without drift. Madhva’s commentary on the same verse was read and differs (indwelt by the Lord, enjoy what He gives), which does not affect this single-commentator entry. entry-check ok.
